LESSON: WHOLE NUMBERS

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade three
Subject: MATHEMATICAL ACTIVITIES
Strand: Numbers
Topic 1.2: Whole Numbers
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 20

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Whole Numbers, part of Numbers in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade three MATHEMATICAL ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: How would you get the total number of people in a group? 2. How do you tell the place value of a digit in a number?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. count numbers forward up to 1000 starting from any point,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Whole Numbers in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. count numbers backward in multiples of 100 from 1000,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Whole Numbers in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Whole Numbers together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Learning to learn: learner counts numbers backward in multiples of 100 from 1000.

● Creativity and Imagination: learners create patterns of numbers up to 1000.

Values:
● Respect: learner gives peers equal opportunity as they take turns to read and write numbers.

● Unity: learner plays games involving whole numbers up to 1000 using digital devices and other resources with peers.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Friendship formation: learner plays games involving whole numbers up to 1000 using digital devices and other resources

with peers.

● Social cohesion: learner discusses place value up to hundreds using place value apparatus in class.

Link to other learning areas:

The learner is able to relate discussion skills to speaking and listening skills in English and Kiswahili Language Activities.
